dataset.name: Tomato-Village (Variant-a, multiclass)
dataset.citation: Gehlot, M., Saxena, R.K. & Gandhi, G.C. (2023). "Tomato-Village": a dataset for end-to-end tomato disease detection in a real-world environment. Multimedia Systems.

models.name: Logistic Regression
models.description: Multinomial (softmax) logistic regression: a linear model that learns one weight vector per class over standardised handcrafted features and turns the class scores into probabilities.
strengths: Fast to train and to run
limitations: Linear decision boundaries in feature space
Only as good as the handcrafted features
Needs scaling and regularisation for high-dimensional HOG vectors

models.name: SVM (RBF kernel)
models.description: Support Vector Machine with an RBF kernel: finds a maximum-margin boundary in an implicit high-dimensional space (kernel trick); C trades margin width against training errors, gamma sets how local each support vector's influence is.
strengths: Non-linear boundaries via the kernel trick
Only support vectors define the model
limitations: Sensitive to C and gamma
Probabilities need extra Platt scaling
Training cost grows quickly with the number of samples

models.name: Random Forest
models.description: Random Forest: an ensemble of decision trees, each trained on a bootstrap sample (bagging) and a random subset of features at every split; the forest averages the trees' votes.
limitations: Large model files
Many weak HOG features dilute the useful colour features
Less effective than kernels on smooth high-dimensional data

models.name: Custom CNN
models.description: A convolutional network trained from scratch: 4 blocks of two 3x3 convolutions + BatchNorm + ReLU and 2x2 max-pooling (32-64-128-256 filters), global average pooling, dropout 0.4 and a linear softmax classifier.
strengths: Learns its own features end to end
limitations: Needs many labelled images; here only ~1,500 training photos
Slower to converge and more prone to overfitting than transfer learning

models.name: MobileNetV2 (feature extraction)
models.description: MobileNetV2 pretrained on ImageNet used as a frozen feature extractor: only the new 8-class head (1280 -> 8) is trained.
strengths: Reuses general visual features learned from 1.2M ImageNet images
limitations: ImageNet features are not specialised for leaf lesions
Backbone cannot adapt to this domain

models.name: MobileNetV2 (fine-tuned)
models.description: MobileNetV2 (inverted residual blocks with depthwise-separable convolutions) pretrained on ImageNet, then fine-tuned end to end with a 10x smaller learning rate after training the head.
strengths: Adapts pretrained features to leaf symptoms
Best use of a small dataset
limitations: More compute-intensive to train than the classical models
Less interpretable than handcrafted features
Trained on leaves photographed on white paper only

models.name: EfficientNet-B0 (fine-tuned)
models.description: EfficientNet-B0 pretrained on ImageNet (compound-scaled MBConv blocks with squeeze-and-excitation), fine-tuned at the native 256x256 resolution with a cosine learning-rate schedule and label smoothing.
limitations: Overfits the small training set quickly
Slower than MobileNetV2 on a CPU

models.name: ConvNeXt-Tiny (fine-tuned)
models.description: ConvNeXt-Tiny pretrained on ImageNet: a modernised ResNet with 7x7 depthwise convolutions, LayerNorm and GELU (28M parameters), fine-tuned at 256x256 with a cosine schedule and label smoothing.
strengths: Strongest pretrained features of the models tried
Large receptive field for lesion patterns
limitations: Largest model here (about 28M parameters)
Slowest to train and to run on a CPU

models.name: ConvNeXt-Tiny (fine-tuned) + TTA
models.feature_set: Learned features; averaged over 8 test-time views
models.description: ConvNeXt-Tiny (fine-tuned) + TTA: the calibrated probabilities of convnext_tiny_v2 are averaged over the 8 flips/rotations of the photo (test-time augmentation).
strengths: Chosen on validation macro-F1 among all candidates
Averaging reduces the variance of single models
A detached leaf has no 'up', so flips/rotations are valid views
limitations: Several forward passes per photo (slower inference)
Less transparent than a single model

selection.criterion: highest validation macro-F1 among all candidates incl. TTA and ensembles (ties: validation accuracy)
reasons: Highest validation macro-F1 of all 15 candidates, including test-time augmentation and ensembles (0.722; runner-up ConvNeXt-Tiny (fine-tuned) 0.718). The test set was not used to choose.
Practical: 211.0 ms per image on CPU, 27.83M parameters.

five_class.rule: Healthy plus the four conditions with the highest validation F1 under the selected 8-class model (validation data only; the test set played no part)

selective.rule: lowest calibrated-confidence threshold with validation accuracy on kept photos >= 95% (coverage >= 50%); chosen on validation, reported once on test

models.name: ConvNeXt-Tiny (5-class) + TTA
models.feature_set: Learned features (ImageNet-pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny, 256px); averaged over 8 test-time views

models.name: EfficientNet-B0 (5-class) + TTA
models.feature_set: Learned features (ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B0, 256px); averaged over 8 test-time views

models.name: Ensemble (5-class): ConvNeXt-Tiny + EfficientNet-B0
models.feature_set: Average of calibrated probabilities: ConvNeXt-Tiny (single view) + EfficientNet-B0 (8-view TTA)

deployment_scope.note: The web app's default model is the focused 5-class model (Healthy plus the four conditions recognised most reliably on validation data). The 8-class models stay available in the model selector.

deployment_check.path: POST /api/predict with each original photo's file bytes (FastAPI TestClient, no explanation)

calibration.threshold_rule: Predictions whose top probability is below 0.60 are shown as 'Uncertain'.
